record.context_brief: Dimension bounds for convex k-orbit polytopes
record.original_question: Determine the number N_k for each k, or improve the known bounds on N_k, where N_k bounds the dimensions in which geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist.

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Determine N_k for every k or improve the bounds for it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A convex polytope P in Euclidean space is called geometrically k-orbit if the symmetry group G(P) (the group of Euclidean isometries preserving P) acts on the set of flags of P (where a flag is a maximal chain F_0 < F_1 < ... < F_{d-1} of nonempty proper faces of P) with exactly k orbits. For each positive integer k, define

  N_k = the smallest integer N (or +∞ if no such integer exists) such that every geometrically k-orbit convex polytope has dimension at most N,

so that geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes can exist only in dimensions d ≤ N_k (with N_k = ∞ meaning they exist in arbitrarily high dimensions).

Problem: For each integer k ≥ 1, determine the exact value of N_k, or otherwise improve the known upper and lower bounds on N_k.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of a list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes. While progress has been made on related questions about k-orbit abstract polytopes (e.g., characterizations via coset geometries), no source found determines N_k exactly for general k or substantially sharpens the bounds in the geometric (convex) setting.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: presents 35 open problems on combinatorial, geometric and algebraic aspects of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.claim: The dimension question for geometrically k-orbit convex polytopes is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: determining whether or not they are empty is still an open problem
status_evidence.claim: Existence of various k-orbit polytope classes remains open, supporting that N_k is not fully determined.
